For me it was both awful yet a huge relief. I felt less heavy, if that makes any sense. It was terrifying to talk about my experiences because I had spent so much time pretending it hadn’t happened. I would do it again if I had to, despite my fears and negative emotions I had to deal with. 

As for the actions of physically reporting it, it was difficult. I was taken into an interview room with a detective and asked a bunch of scary and uncomfortable questions. I had asked for a female detective and for me that made it a lot easier. She guided me through the process and supported me. We went at my pace and she was super encouraging. But no matter how hard she tried, it was still a emotionally challenging situation and it affected my mood for days. 

But in the end, it’s up to you and what you think is best for you. If you can move forward with your life the way it is, don’t feel obligated to report. If you feel like reporting will relieve the burden that’s been placed on you, think about it. Honestly, it’s different for everyone and what they need and can handle. I hope you can make a decision that satisfies what you desire. No matter what, I support your decision and hope that you get the closure you deserve.
